decided.claim: Reveal via the FreeDesktop org.freedesktop.FileManager1.ShowItems DBus method (Nautilus/Nemo/Caja and similar), shelled out through dbus-send rather than adding a DBus client crate; on failure (no bus, no dbus-send, unsupporting file manager) fall back to opening the parent directory with the existing open_with_system.

reveal_with_system runs the dbus-send call and its fallback on a plain std::thread::spawn background thread rather than cx.background_executor(), so it stays a free function with no Context dependency, callable identically from the mouse handler and the context menu, matching this file's existing std::thread::spawn idiom for detached blocking work.

Super+Ctrl-click is ev.modifiers.platform && ev.modifiers.control (verified against gpui's Modifiers struct, where platform is documented as 'the super key, on linux'), checked ahead of the existing Shift/Ctrl branch; a click with nothing to reveal falls through to that branch unchanged so Ctrl alone still opens. Shift's state is not part of the reveal test.

file_uri_to_path only resolves a reveal target when the URI's authority is empty or localhost; any other host is treated as not on this disk and yields None, never attempting a reveal or a fallback open.

Hand-rolled percent_decode/percent_encode_path instead of a new crate dependency (no percent-encoding/url crate is in Cargo.toml); the encoder also escapes ',' because dbus-send's own array:string: argument syntax splits array elements on an unescaped comma.

Factored link_under's grid-walk-and-classify logic out into classify_link_under so the new reveal_under reuses the identical click-to-token-to-Link pipeline instead of re-deriving it; link_under's own behaviour is unchanged.

Added a 'Reveal in file manager  ↗' row directly beneath 'Open link  ↗' in the right-click menu, shown only when reveal_under resolves for the position the menu opened at, so a web URL still offers only Open.

Built the dbus-send argv with Command::args(Vec<String>), never a shell string, so no path or filename content is ever interpreted by a shell -- this, not ad hoc escaping, is what makes spaces/commas/other awkward characters safe.

least_confident.why: ShowItems is my best knowledge of the standard cross-desktop reveal mechanism (it's what VS Code uses on Linux), but there is no running D-Bus session or file manager in this sandbox to confirm it actually selects the item, or that dbus-send's exit code is non-zero on every failure mode the fallback relies on.

The platform field is confirmed correct for Super from gpui's own source, but several Linux compositors/window managers reserve bare Super or Super+chord combinations for their own global shortcuts before an app's window ever sees the event -- untestable without a live compositor session.

Treating a non-empty, non-localhost file:// authority as unrevealable is a judgment call with no evidence either way of what an agent's Links table would ever print there, since it always names the same machine the pane runs on.

not_done.claim: A bare absolute path containing a literal, un-encoded space in the printed terminal text is still not detected as a link at all.
not_done.why: Pre-existing limitation of link_at's whitespace tokenizer, which this ticket says to build on rather than re-derive; fixing it means redesigning token-boundary detection, disproportionate to this ask. The brief's own space example is satisfied for the shape agents actually print one in -- a file:// URI with %20.

not_done.claim: ftp://, ftps:// and mailto: links are treated as non-revealable, same as http(s).
not_done.why: Only 'a bare absolute path and a file:// URI' are named as target shapes in the brief; erred toward not offering reveal on anything not explicitly in scope rather than guessing at ftp-as-local-path semantics.
